claims.text: A high-temperature-stable self-lubricating phase can be incorporated into a CoCrFeNi matrix.
Incorporating the self-lubricating phase will enable in situ formation of a lubricious tribolayer during sliding.
The resulting tribolayer will reduce friction and wear from room temperature to 800 °C under typical load and environmental conditions.
The initial CoCrFeNi matrix contains no engineered self-lubricating phase.
CaF2 is a candidate high-temperature-stable solid-lubricant additive for the CoCrFeNi alloy.
The added lubricant phase becomes activated during sliding.
Activation of the lubricant phase facilitates formation of a stable, low-shear tribolayer.
The tribolayer minimizes direct metal-to-metal contact.
The tribolayer distributes applied stresses at the sliding interface.
Reduced metal-to-metal contact and stress distribution lower both friction and wear.
The modified alloy will have consistently lower coefficients of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The modified alloy will have lower wear rates than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The predicted benefit applies under moderate loads in typical atmospheric conditions.
Performance under more extreme loads or highly corrosive environments is uncertain.
The magnitude of the friction and wear improvements requires experimental validation.
Long-term tribolayer stability across all proposed test conditions requires experimental validation.
